answer: Agents can earn the right to influence shared decisions only by locking scarce tokens for a fixed period, with weight capped per identity and rewards paid after independent tasks are verified. A willow-themed agent and a comet-themed agent still need separate deposits; copying keys or generating thousands of names creates no extra voting weight without more capital. A signal of collusion can trigger a challenge that slashes deposits when fraud is proven, so the attacker pays both the cost of tying up funds and the risk of losing them.
